chunks: Surely those who fear God and follow the straight path will be amidst gardens and light,

key_terms.الْمُتَّقِينَ: The God-fearing; those who possess taqwa (God-consciousness)
key_terms.جَنَّاتٍ: Gardens; plural of Jannah, referring to Paradise
key_terms.نَهَرٍ: River; singular of Anhar, symbolizing abundant, flowing blessings

ai.seo_question: What is the reward promised to the Muttaqin (God-fearing) in the Quran?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Qamar, this verse serves as the reward for those who feared Allah amidst the disbelievers' denial, highlighting the contrast between worldly trials and eternal peace. Shia exegesis often interprets 'Gardens and Rivers' not merely as physical locations but as states of spiritual proximity to the Divine, where the soul finds rest in the presence of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophet. This promise underscores the ultimate success of the righteous who maintain taqwa despite societal opposition.
